After completing this lesson, you will be able to set up your development environment for creating mobile AI applications, including installing Android Studio and Xcode, and setting up a dedicated folder for your portfolio project. This foundational step is crucial for your role as a Mobile AI Developer, as it ensures you have the necessary tools to start building and testing AI features on both Android and iOS platforms from day one.

## What you'll do

In this lesson, you will use a **Browser** to navigate to official documentation and guides to set up your development environment. You will download and install **Android Studio** and **Xcode**, and create a new project in both. Additionally, you will create a dedicated folder named `playground` in your project directory to house your portfolio project. This setup will prepare you to start coding and experimenting with AI features in your mobile applications.

"Done" means you have successfully installed Android Studio and Xcode, created a new project in both, and set up a `playground` folder in your file structure.

## Setting Up Android Studio

### Downloading and Installing Android Studio

Imagine Android Studio as a powerful toolbox for crafting Android applications. Just as a carpenter needs the right tools to build a sturdy and beautiful cabinet, a Mobile AI Developer needs Android Studio to design and develop robust applications. To get started, visit the official Android Studio website at <https://developer.android.com/studio> and download the latest version of Android Studio. The process is straightforward and can be broken down into a few simple steps:

1. **Navigate to the Download Page**: Go to the Android Studio download page and select the "Stable" version, as it provides a stable and tested environment for development.
2. **Choose the Installation Type**: Select the "Custom" installation type to ensure you only install the components you need. This helps in keeping the installation lightweight and focused on your project requirements.
3. **Install the Components**: During the installation, ensure you check the boxes next to "Android SDK" and "Google Play Services" as these are essential for building and testing mobile applications.
4. **Launch Android Studio**: Once installed, launch Android Studio and follow the on-screen instructions to set up your workspace.

```text
> [!TIP] Make sure to create a separate user account in Android Studio for each project to avoid conflicts between different projects.
```

### Creating a New Project

After setting up Android Studio, the next step is to create a new project. Think of this process as selecting the blueprint for your cabinet. The project template provides a starting point for your application, and you can modify it to fit your needs.

1. **Open Android Studio**: Launch the application and select "Start a new Android Studio project" from the welcome screen.
2. **Choose the Project Template**: For a Mobile AI Developer, selecting the "Empty Activity" template is a good starting point. This template provides a basic structure for you to build upon.
3. **Configure the Project**: Fill in the details such as the project name, location, and package name. Ensure you select the appropriate language (Java or Kotlin) and the minimum API level required for your target audience.
4. **Finish the Setup**: Click "Finish" to complete the setup. Android Studio will create the project structure and open the project in the IDE.

```java
// Example: Creating a new project in Android Studio
// Open Android Studio and start a new Android Studio project.
// Choose "Empty Activity" as the project template.
// Configure the project details, such as the project name, location, and package name.
// Ensure the correct language and minimum API level are selected.
// Finish the setup by clicking "Finish".
```

> [!QUESTION] What are the key components to check during the Android Studio installation process?
>
> > [!ANSWER] During the installation process, ensure you check the boxes next to "Android SDK" and "Google Play Services" to include these essential components.

## Understanding Xcode Basics

### Downloading and Installing Xcode

Xcode is Apple’s official IDE for developing iOS and macOS applications. It is a comprehensive environment that includes everything you need to build, test, and distribute your apps. Think of Xcode as a full-service kitchen in your development studio, offering all the tools you need to cook up a delicious digital dish.

To download Xcode, visit the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/xcode/id497799835). Once you have installed Xcode, you can start setting up your development environment.

### Creating a New Project

To create a new project in Xcode, follow these steps:

1. **Open Xcode**: Launch the Xcode application.
2. **Create a New Project**: Select "File" > "New" > "Project" from the menu bar. A dialog will appear.
3. **Choose a Template**: In the "Project Navigator" on the left, select "iOS" and then "App".
4. **Configure the Project**: Fill in the details such as the project name, team, and language. Xcode supports both Swift and Objective-C, so choose the one that best fits your needs.
5. **Location and Packaging**: Specify the location where you want to save your project and the organization identifier (bundle identifier).
6. **Finish the Setup**: Click "Create" to complete the setup. Xcode will create the project structure and open the project in the IDE.

```swift
// Example: Creating a new project in Xcode
// Open Xcode and select "File" > "New" > "Project".
// Choose "iOS" and then "App" as the project template.
// Configure the project details, such as the project name, team, and language.
// Specify the location and organization identifier.
// Finish the setup by clicking "Create".
```

> [!TIP] It’s a good practice to use a consistent naming convention for your projects, especially when working on multiple apps. This helps avoid confusion and makes it easier to manage your codebase.

### Self-Check

> [!QUESTION] What are the key components to check during the Xcode installation process?

> [!ANSWER] During the installation process, ensure you check the boxes next to "Command Line Tools" to include the necessary command-line tools for building and running your projects.

## Creating a Playground Folder

### Why a Dedicated Folder?

Creating a dedicated folder for your portfolio project is like building a workspace for a specific project. Just as a carpenter has a designated area for tools and materials, having a structured folder for your project helps maintain organization and clarity. This makes it easier to manage your code, resources, and documentation, ensuring that everything is easy to find and understand.

### Setting Up the Folder

To set up the folder, follow these steps:

1. **Choose a Location**: Select a location that is easily accessible and organized. For example, you might choose a folder named "AIProjects" in your Documents folder.
2. **Create the Main Folder**: Inside the main folder, create a subfolder for your portfolio project. For instance, name it "MobileAIApp".
3. **Organize the Structure**: Inside "MobileAIApp", create subfolders for different components of your project:
    - **Code**: Store all your source code here.
    - **Resources**: Store images, fonts, and other resources.
    - **Documentation**: Keep all documentation related to the project.
    - **Tests**: Place unit tests and integration tests here.

Here is an example of how the folder structure might look:

```text
AIProjects
├── MobileAIApp
│   ├── Code
│   │   ├── Android
│   │   │   ├── src
│   │   │   └── gradle
│   │   └── iOS
│   │       ├── Sources
│   │       └── Resources
│   ├── Resources
│   ├── Documentation
│   └── Tests
```

### Example

Let's walk through the creation of this structure in a concrete example. Suppose you are creating an AI app that integrates LLMs and on-device models.

1. **Main Location**: You decide to place the project in your Documents folder.
2. **Main Folder**: Create a folder named "AIProjects".
3. **Project Folder**: Inside "AIProjects", create a folder named "MobileAIApp".
4. **Subfolders**: Inside "MobileAIApp", create the following subfolders:
    - **Code**: For Android and iOS code.
    - **Resources**: For any images or other resources.
    - **Documentation**: For any documentation related to the project.
    - **Tests**: For any tests you might write.

### Self-Check

> [!QUESTION] What are the benefits of creating a dedicated folder structure for your portfolio project?

> [!ANSWER] The benefits include easier management of code and resources, better organization, and clarity when working on the project.

## Try it yourself

### 1. Setting Up Android Studio

> [!TIP] If you don't have a Google account, you can still download and install Android Studio.

1. Go to the official Android Studio website: <https://developer.android.com/studio>.
2. Click on the "Download" button and select the "Stable" version.
3. Choose the appropriate download for your operating system (Windows, macOS, or Linux).
4. Once the download is complete, run the installer and follow the on-screen instructions.
5. After installation, launch Android Studio.
6. Create a new project by selecting "Start a new Android Studio project" from the welcome screen.
7. Choose a template (e.g., "Empty Activity").
8. Click "Next" and name your project (e.g., "AIProjects").
9. Select the minimum SDK version and click "Finish".

> [!NOTE] The project will now be created in a default location, such as `~/AndroidStudioProjects`.

### 2. Understanding Xcode Basics

> [!TIP] If you don't have a Mac, you can use a virtual machine or a cloud-based Mac to install Xcode.

1. Go to the official Xcode download page: <https://developer.apple.com/xcode/>.
2. Click on "Download Xcode" and log in with your Apple ID if prompted.
3. Once Xcode is downloaded, open it.
4. From the Xcode menu, select `File` > `New` > `Project`.
5. Choose "App" under the "iOS" template and click "Next".
6. Name your project (e.g., "AIProjects").
7. Choose a Swift or Objective-C language and click "Next".
8. Select a location to save your project and click "Create".

### 3. Creating a Playground Folder

1. Open your file explorer (Windows File Explorer, macOS Finder, or Linux file manager).
2. Navigate to your Documents folder.
3. Create a new folder named "AIProjects".
4. Inside "AIProjects", create the following subfolders:
    - **Code**: For Android and iOS code.
    - **Resources**: For any images or other resources.
    - **Documentation**: For any documentation related to the project.
    - **Tests**: For any tests you might write.

> [!NOTE] Your folder structure should now look like this:

```text
AIProjects
├── Code
├── Resources
├── Documentation
└── Tests
```

### Self-Check

> [!QUESTION] What are the benefits of creating a dedicated folder structure for your portfolio project?

> [!ANSWER] The benefits include easier management of code and resources, better organization, and clarity when working on the project.

### Common mistakes

- **Not using a dedicated folder structure:** This can lead to disorganized code and resources, making it harder to find and manage files. To avoid this, always create a structured folder for your project.
- **Forgetting to install necessary tools:** Missing tools can cause errors and delays in development. Ensure you have installed both Android Studio and Xcode, and that they are properly set up.

### Recap

- **Installed Android Studio:** Downloaded and set up Android Studio for Android development.
- **Installed Xcode:** Downloaded and set up Xcode for iOS development.
- **Created a Playground Folder:** Set up a dedicated folder structure for your portfolio project.
- **Understood the folder structure:** Created subfolders for code, resources, documentation, and tests.
- **Know the benefits of structured folders:** Easier management, better organization, and clarity when working on the project.
